human_tolerance.notes: Visits cultivated potato and artichoke fields and eats garbage (Wikipedia, Diet). Urban affinity is judgement.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Farrowing occurs between March and May (Wikipedia: Reproduction).

vocalizations.description: Grunting noises that differ in intensity by situation (Wikipedia: Vocalisation). Adult males are usually silent; females grunt often and piglets whine. Feeding boars purr.
Loud huffing 'ukh! ukh!' sounds or screeches (transcribed 'gu-gu-gu') when frightened (Wikipedia: Vocalisation).
High-pitched, piercing combat cries (Wikipedia: Vocalisation). Timing of combat is not dated in the source, so the call is not restricted to months.

external.note: GBIF usage key 7705930 and iNaturalist taxon 42134 checked on 2026-10-31 (GBIF species/match and iNaturalist taxa API: accepted species rank). iNaturalist, NCBI (9823) and GBIF ids agree with Wikidata P3151, P685 and P846. ITIS TSN 180722 is the species; the subspecies Sus scrofa scrofa (TSN 898310) is not used.

common_names.note: Labels en 'wild boar', fr 'sanglier', de 'Wildschwein' from Wikidata Q58697.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern (Q211005); Wikipedia also states least concern.

range.note: native FR is derived from Wikipedia's statement that the species is native to much of Eurasia; no per-country native list is given, so no other native countries are asserted. Introduced countries are cited to specific passages in Wikipedia: AR and UY (introduced for breeding in the 20th century), BR (large-scale creation of wild boar and hybrids from the mid-1990s), US (boars released from zoos and farms), AU (feral pig and boar-hybrid pest). Invasive US and AU follow the article's description of serious pest populations in the Americas and Australia. Other countries need a per-country source before a locale uses them.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walk and gallop from the Description (maximum run 40 km/h); swim from Habitat (competent swimmers). Trot is not sourced and is omitted.

traits.thermoregulation.note: Mammal; endothermy is a class-level fact.

traits.size_class.note: Large: mass_kg 78.75 is above the 50 kg Medium/Large boundary.

traits.mass_kg.note: Mean of the midpoints of the male (75-100 kg, midpoint 87.5 kg) and female (60-80 kg, midpoint 70 kg) averages given for most of Europe in Wikipedia (Description). Averages vary with region; Mediterranean averages are lower.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Lower bound 45 kg (Mediterranean female average) and upper bound 100 kg (top of the male European average) from Wikipedia (Description). These are regional average ends, not individual extremes.

traits.length_m.note: Mean of male (150 cm) and female (140 cm) body length in most of Europe (Wikipedia: Description), converted to m.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Mean of male (75-80 cm, midpoint 77.5 cm) and female (70 cm) shoulder height in most of Europe (Wikipedia: Description), converted to m and rounded.

traits.speed_ms.note: Gallop 11.1 m/s derived from the maximum 40 km/h (Wikipedia: Description) divided by 3.6.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia: few survive past 4-5 years; maximum in the wild 10-14 years. The value 5 is the typical end of a wild life, not the maximum.

traits.diet.note: Judgement: Wikipedia (Diet) describes the food categories and says acorns and beechnuts are the most important items in temperate zones, but gives no proportions. Shares are authored to approximate that ordering and sum to 1. Invertebrate and carrion are warm-period items in the source.

traits.social.note: Structure Group: Wikipedia (Social behaviour and life cycle) describes female-dominated sounders led by an old matriarch. Group size range [3, 20] is judgement; the source gives no size.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Judgement, not sourced. Wikipedia contains no diel activity statement (searched for night, dusk, dawn, daytime, diurnal, crepuscular). The FR activity curve in activity.regions is monthly and effort-corrected, so it cannot establish a daily pattern. Cathemeral is kept as the authored label and should be revisited if a diel source is found.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: Flee is the main response. Wikipedia (Attacks) describes charging when a boar is cornered or threatened, which is recorded in the notes rather than as Mob.

traits.wariness.note: judgement: no source gives a wariness value; authored for the flee-first response.

habitat.use.note: Ground use from Habitat and sheltering; boars root and forage on the ground. Judgement for the 1.0 share.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Wikipedia (Habitat and sheltering): shelters in tall grass or shrub thickets, with insulating material.

habitat.resources.note: Weights are judgement. Mast (acorns, beechnuts) is the most important temperate food (Wikipedia: Diet). The months for mast follow autumn fall (Wikipedia: nuts and seeds dug from under snow); invertebrates and carrion are warm-period items. Rhizomes, roots and tubers, the main year-round food, have no resource tag in the schema, so they are not represented.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Judgement for urban_affinity Adapter. Wikipedia reports boars visiting cultivated potato and artichoke fields and eating garbage (Diet). Other values are not asserted.

seasonal.strategy.note: Active year round: Wikipedia does not describe hibernation or torpor; boars are active in winter (Diet: digs up food from under snow).

seasonal.phases.note: Farrowing March to May (Wikipedia: Reproduction). Rut timing is not dated in the source, so no rut phase is written.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile duration 365 days derived from sows reaching sexual maturity at one year (Wikipedia). The scale 0.6 is judgement.

vocalizations.note: Call types and descriptions follow Wikipedia (Vocalisation: contact grunts, alarm huffs, high-pitched combat cries). Cooldowns and loudness are judgement; no call recordings are linked.

look.note: Judgement: block-mesh proportions, palette, snout colour and tusk placement are authored, not measured. Wikipedia (Description) supports a massive body, large head, short legs, short neck, dark bristly adult coat and prominent canine tusks in males. Tusk offset and size are fractions of the snout box in the previewer's extra-part convention; positions were checked visually in the previewer.

behavior.note: Program fsm-ground-forager-v1 fits a ground-foraging mammal that rests, flees and drinks. Parameters are judgement. food_tag 'mast' is chosen because mast is the most important temperate food; the off-season (no mast) boar wanders. Rooting is not representable.
